predecessors.name: Former Qin
predecessors.text: the Hebei plain and Beijing, which Murong Chui held from his revolt of 384

successors.name: Northern Yan
successors.text: the Longcheng remnant under Gao Yun and Feng Ba

ledger.x: 384: Murong Chui rebels against Former Qin and founds Later Yan.
385: Goguryeo invades Later Yan.
385: the page names the invasion and no later year, so the contest closes with it.
385: Later Yan takes Ye and most of Hebei from Former Qin.
386: Murong Chui makes Zhongshan his capital (8 February) and takes the imperial title (15 February).
392: Murong Chui destroys Zhai Wei.
394: Murong Chui conquers Western Yan.
394: Later Yan takes Shandong from the Jin.
396: Murong Chui leads a campaign against Wei and dies; the Wei invade.
396 (fall): the Wei attack Bing Province.
397: Murong Bao abandons Zhongshan.
397: the capital moves from Zhongshan to Longcheng (Chaoyang, Liaoning); infobox Longcheng 397-409.
398: the Wei hold most of Later Yan.
398: Murong Bao is assassinated by Lan Han and Murong De founds Southern Yan.
398: the fighting for Hebei ends with Later Yan at Longcheng.
400: Later Yan attacks Goguryeo.
404: Goguryeo takes Liaodong.
406: the Liaodong fighting ends with Goguryeo in possession.

407: Murong Yun (Gao Yun) kills Murong Xi at Fu Xunying's funeral (16 September 407) and takes the throne; "Feng Ba replaced him on the throne, thus ending the Later Yan and beginning the Northern Yan" on that page's own dating.
409: Gao Yun is assassinated and Feng Ba takes the throne; the state passes to the Northern Yan.

wars.name: Goguryeo invasion of Later Yan
wars.outcome: Gogukyang of Goguryeo invaded Later Yan in 385; the page gives no result and no later year.

wars.name: Later Yan-Goguryeo wars of Gwanggaeto
wars.outcome: 400: Later Yan attacked Goguryeo and was repulsed; 402: Goguryeo took the fortress Sukgunseong near the Later Yan capital; 404: Later Yan lost Liaodong to Goguryeo (Later Yan page); 405 and 406: Later Yan attacked Goguryeo's Liaodong fortresses and was…

wars.name: Later Yan-Zhai Wei war
wars.outcome: Zhai Wei founded at Huatai in 388 and destroyed by Murong Chui in 392.

wars.name: Later Yan conquest of Western Yan
wars.outcome: Zhangzi besieged, Murong Yong captured and killed; Western Yan ended.

wars.name: Northern Wei-Later Yan war
wars.outcome: Canhe Slope (8 December 395) routed Later Yan; Murong Chui's 396 campaign failed; Zhongshan evacuated 27 April 397; by 398 the Wei held most of the state's land.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Wei, Goguryeo and Southern Yan frontiers are named by city and province, not by line.
